r.정치 구도: The president is directly elected, but day-to-day government is run by a prime minister and cabinet who need the confidence of the lower house, making it a parliamentary system. The 1989 Velvet Revolution brought down communist rule, and in 1993 the country split peacefully from Slovakia. In the October 2025 election, the populist ANO party, long a critic of the established parties, came first and formed a coalition with the anti-immigration right-wing SPD and a party campaigning for motorists' interests. The new government put Czechia first, saying it would not spend state money on arms for Ukraine. It did, however, agree to keep running the Czech-led ammunition initiative as long as other countries pay for it. Conflict-of-interest questions over the large business group the prime minister founded have been a long-running issue.

t.why: A landlocked country surrounded by Germany, Poland, Austria and Slovakia, it joined NATO in 1999 and the European Union in 2004, but uses its own currency, the koruna, rather than the euro. Memories of the 1968 Prague Spring being crushed by Soviet-led troops keep public opinion wary of Russia. During the war in Ukraine it drew attention by leading an effort to find artillery shells around the world and buy them for Ukraine. Its economy is tightly bound to the German car industry, so it feels German downturns and Europe's shift to electric vehicles almost at once. Because nuclear power supplies a large share of its electricity, its plans for new reactors are a regular part of European energy news.
t.rel: The Czech Republic and Slovakia split peacefully in 1993. It is a NATO and EU member, and its car industry is deeply tied to the German economy.
t.korea: South Korea established relations with what was then Czechoslovakia in March 1990 and has kept ties with the Czech Republic since the 1993 split. Hyundai Motor has built cars at its Nošovice plant since 2008, its only production base inside the European Union. In June 2025, Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power signed a contract to build two reactors at Dukovany, after a court lifted a temporary block on the signing that followed a challenge to the tender by France's EDF. Construction is meant to start in 2029, with the first unit running in 2036. In November 2026, KHNP ended construction talks with a group of Korean builders and began looking for a new contractor, raising questions about whether the schedule will hold.
t.know: Czechs drink more beer per person than anyone else in the world.
etext: Manufacturing makes up one of the largest shares of GDP in Europe. It builds cars, car parts and machinery, selling most of them to the European Union and above all to Germany. A long industrial tradition and skilled workers are its strengths.
Defense companies making ammunition, armored vehicles and small arms have grown quickly since the war in Ukraine. Rising defense budgets across Europe are creating new demand.
It has long drawn much of its electricity from nuclear and coal, and plans more nuclear power as it phases down coal. It moved quickly to switch gas suppliers to cut its reliance on Russia.

Its heavy reliance on the German economy means it suffers when Germany does. Workers are in short supply, and because much of its industry is assembly, raising the share of research and high-value work is a challenge.
